lines.li: [them] A traveler at our fire spoke of your colony, and the young ones listened.
[us] What did the traveler say?
[them] That your camp is {RENOWN}, and that it keeps its word.
[them] Your colony came up at our market last week.
[us] For good or ill?
[them] Good, mostly, though the cheese seller had opinions.
[them] People back home have started asking about your settlement.
[us] What do you tell them?
[them] That it's {RENOWN}, and worth the walk.
[them] Your colony turns up on our settlement's channel now and then.
[us] Is that good?
[them] It means people have noticed you, which out here is rare.
[them] Your colony is {RENOWN}, I'm told.
[us] We hadn't heard.
[them] The nobility rarely tells anyone what it thinks of them.
[them] The elders tell of your colony at our fire, and the children ask for it again.
[us] I hope they tell it kindly.
[them] Kindly enough, and a little longer each time.
[them] There's a song about your colony in our hall now, if you can believe it.
[us] Is it a good one?
[them] The tune's good, and most of the words are true.
[them] Your settlement made the papers back home.
[us] Page one, I hope.
[them] Page two, but it's a good page.
[them] Your colony's name comes up on every channel in the region.
[us] In a good way, I hope.
[them] In a way that makes people stop and listen.
[them] At court one hears your colony spoken of now and then.
[us] What do they say?
[them] That it is worth knowing, which at court is high praise.
[them] My town would welcome any of your people at its table.
[us] That's kind of you.
[them] It's sense, a colony with a name like yours is worth having near.
[them] Even people who've never seen your colony know its name.
[us] That's strange to hear.
[them] Your colony is {RENOWN}, so get used to it.
[them] Clans we have never met tell of your camp now.
[us] Then I hope they tell it true.
[them] True enough, and better every winter.
[them] Your colony is sung of in halls I'll never see.
[us] We haven't heard the songs ourselves.
[them] Then you'll have to come and listen one day.
[them] Every people within reach seems to know your colony by now.
[us] We only wanted to be left in peace.
[them] A known name keeps the peace better than walls do, most days.
[them] Your colony is {RENOWN}, did you know?
[us] We didn't, and I'm not sure what to make of it.
[them] Make use of it, that is what the court would do.
[them] I'd not heard of your colony before I came here.
[us] We keep to ourselves, mostly.
[them] Then I'll be the first at home to tell of it.
[them] Among us a camp earns its name by what its people do for others.
[us] Then ours is still earning.
[them] Good, the earning is the best part.
[them] Your settlement isn't on any list I've seen.
[us] Is that bad?
[them] It's quiet, and quiet has its uses.
[them] Your colony's known for {KNOWNFOR} where I come from.
[us] We've had to be.
[them,their:tribal] Our young hunters want to wrestle one of you to see.
[them] Some of our young ones want to try their luck against one of you.
[them] Our captain says your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and he doesn't praise easily.
[us] Tell him thank you.
[them] He'd say there's nothing to thank him for.
[them] A colony known for {KNOWNFOR} might find its people welcome in the Empire's ranks.
[us] We're needed here.
[them] A pity, the Empire rewards its soldiers well.
[them] They say your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and people remember who healed them.
[us] We do what we can for anyone hurt.
[them] That's why they remember.
[them] Our healer has heard that your camp is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Maybe the two of them could trade what they know.
[them] Our healer would like that, if the elders allow it.
[them] Our medics say your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We've had a lot of practice, sadly.
[them] Practice is how anyone gets good.
[them] Your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and I can see why.
[us] Sit down, then, there's room.
[them,their:lowtech] I'll sit, and gladly.
[them] Don't mind if I do.
[them] On the road they say your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] We try to feed whoever comes.
[them] Then I'll tell them it's true, and that I ate well.
[them] Your colony's known for {KNOWNFOR}, I'm told.
[us] Fair, I hope you were told.
[them] Fair, and hard to get the better of.
[them] Your colony's known for {KNOWNFOR}, it's in our trade notes.
[us] Is that good or bad for us?
[them] Good for you, bad for our margins.
[them] Your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}, and I'd like to see some of it.
[us] Look around, a fair bit of what's here is our own work.
[them] I'm looking.
[them] Our crafters say your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] They're welcome to come and see how we work.
[them] They'll want to, and to trade a trick or two.
[them] Your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}, even among us.
[us,samefaith] Then we pray to the same, and that's good company.
[us] We keep to what we believe, that's all.
[them] That's more than most manage.
[them] People of faith we meet on the road ask about your colony.
[us] They'd be welcome here.
[them] I'll tell them so.
[them] Your colony's name isn't a good one where I come from.
[us] People say a lot of things.
[them] They say this one often.
[them] I'd rather not be seen talking with one of your colony.
[us] Then walk on.
[them] Your colony has a name for trouble, but you seem all right.
[us] Most of us are.
[them] Then maybe the name will change.
[them,their:tribal] At our fire your camp is a story told to frighten children.
[them,their:medieval] In our hall your colony's name is said low, and not kindly.
[them,their:hightech] Your settlement is {RENOWN}, you know.
[us] Then we have work to do.
[them] You do, and people will watch you do it.
[them] Wait, you're {KNOWNAS}, aren't you?
[us] That's what they call me, I suppose.
[them] Then I'll tell them at home I met you.
[them] At home they speak of you as {KNOWNAS}.
[us] I didn't know anyone spoke of me at all.
[them,their:lowtech] They do, by the fire, when the young ones ask for a story.
[them] They do, more often than you'd think.
[them] So this is {KNOWNAS}.
[us,trait:Kind] It wasn't only me, the whole colony was there.
[us] I only did what anyone here would have done.
[them] Maybe, but you're the one they name.
[them] Our fighters know your name, they'd like a bout with you one day.
[us] A friendly one, I hope.
[them,their:tribal] Friendly, then a feast, as it should be.
[them] Friendly enough, they mean to learn from you.
[them] You're the healer they talk about, aren't you?
[us] I've tended a few people, yes.
[them] Some of them are back on their feet because of you.
[them] Travelers say you're the one who makes guests feel at home here.
[us] Someone has to put the kettle on.
[them] Then I'm glad it's you.
[them] Our traders know your name, and they warned me about you.
[us] Warned you?
[them] That you strike a fair bargain and never a soft one.
[them] People at home know your work before they know your face.
[us] Better that way round, my face is nothing much.
[them] Your work is, though.
[them] They say you keep the rites at your colony better than anyone.
[us] Somebody has to remember how they go.
[them] Then your colony is lucky to have you.
[them] You are spoken of at court as {KNOWNAS}.
[us] I hope that's a compliment there.
[them] At court, being spoken of at all is the compliment.
[them] Your colony is {RENOWN}, and you're part of the reason.
[us] Everyone here is part of the reason.
[them] Spoken like one of them.
[them] The fighting with {THEN} still goes on, you know.
[us] I'd hoped it was over.
[them] Some at home say a colony known for {KNOWNFOR} would end it quicker.
[us] We have our own walls to watch.
[us] Is that business with {THEN} over now?
[them] Over, and people at home have gone back to talking about other things.
[us] Such as?
[them] Your colony, for one.
[them] The war with {THEN} is over, you'll be glad to hear.
[us] I am, for all your sakes.
[them] Our young ones had hoped to fight beside a colony known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[them] The war with {THEN} is over at last.
[us] I'm glad to hear it.
[them] Peace gives people time to listen, and they ask for news of your colony.
[us] Has {THEN} let up at home?
[them] Not yet, and some there talk of walking all the way here for your colony's help.
[us] Tell them the gate is open to the sick.
[them] {THEN} has passed at home, I'm glad to say.
[us] That's a relief.
[them] Some said if it hadn't, they'd have come to your colony for its {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] How is {THEN} doing?
[them] Holding on, and asking about your colony's healers whenever I visit.
[us] Is {THEN} on the mend?
[them] Back on their feet, I'm glad to say.
[us] Good, and if it comes back, bring them here.
[them] I would, your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}, after all.
[them] {NOW} leads us now, and asked me about your colony before I left.
[us] What did you tell them?
[them] The truth, mostly.
[us] Does {THEN} still lead your people?
[them] Still, and {THEN} has heard of your colony by now.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them] Good enough, from what I hear.
[them] Our town has a new head now, {NOW}.
[us] Does {NOW} know of us?
[them] Of your colony, at least, its name gets around.
[them] Our town has a new head now, {NOW}.
[us] Has {NOW} heard of us?
[them] Of your colony, yes, and not kindly, I'm afraid.
[us] Is {THEN} still at the head of your town?
[them] Still, and even {THEN} knows of your colony by now.
[us] How did the harvest go, in the end?
[them] Well enough, though nobody at home sets a table like your colony's.
[us] You'll have to come back and eat with us, then.
[us] Is {THEN} still going on?
[them] Still, and a colony known for {KNOWNFOR} is a good thought in lean times.
[us] Our door's open if anyone needs a meal.
[them] {THEN} is over now, I'm glad to say.
[us] That's good to hear.
[them] Now people have time to talk of other things, your colony among them.
[us] Is {THEN} still on at home?
[them] Still, and a colony known for {KNOWNFOR} is a warm thought on cold nights.
[us] Come and warm up with us, then.
[us] Did that trade you mentioned come to anything?
[them] Some, but our traders say they'd rather deal with your colony.
[us] Then send them our way.
[us] It's been a while since we spoke of trade.
[them] It has, and our traders still ask after a colony known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Then send them our way.
[us] How's that work of yours coming along?
[them] Slowly, and I keep hearing your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Come and see some of it, then.
[them] We spoke of work last time, and I've thought of your colony's {KNOWNFOR} since.
[us] Come and see it whenever you like.
[them] I'll hold you to that.
[them] I've thought about our talk of faith, and that your colony is known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Faith is easier with others beside you.
[them] It is, and I'm glad to have met some of yours.
[us] Did {THEN} ever settle down?
[them] It did, and now people at home have time to gossip about places like yours.
[us] I'm not sure I like the sound of that.
[us] Is {THEN} still going on at home?
[them] Still, so it's good to sit a while in a colony known for {KNOWNFOR}.
[us] Sit as long as you like.
[us] Is {THEN} still going on?
[them] Still, and some at home say a colony like yours would know what to do.
[us] I wish we did.
[us] Is {THEN} still at the head of your town?
[them] Still, and {THEN} asked after you by name before I left.
[us] By name?
[them] As {KNOWNAS}, which is near enough.
[them] You asked after my family last time, so I'll ask after your colony.
[us] We're well enough, all of us.
[them] Good, people at home ask after it now.
[us] How is your family keeping?
[them] Well, and they'd like to hear I sat with your colony's people out here.
[us] Now you can say you have.
[us] Is the fighting with {THEN} still going on?
[them] Still, and people at home wonder which side your colony would take.
[us] Our own, as long as we can.
[them] I put in that good word for you, as I said I would.
[us] Thank you, did it land?
[them] Your colony's name did most of the work.
[them] On the road here people asked where I was going.
[us] And when you told them?
[them] Some knew your colony by name, and wished me a good visit.
[them] Since that raid we talked about, have things been quieter?
[us] A little.
[them] People at home say your colony brings trouble on itself, I'm sorry to say.
[us] Did the harvest come in?
[them] It did, and at the market people asked whether your colony had any to sell.
[us] Tell them to come and ask us themselves.
[them] About that favour we spoke of.
[us] Yes?
[them] My people would sooner owe your colony than most, given its name.
[them] {THEN} is well again, and asked me to thank the colony's healers.
[us] Tell them we're glad.
[them] They asked after you in particular.
